capabilities: Masks completed words as glyphs while typing
Reveals masked text on selection, hover or caret click
Masks targeted words, phrases and sensitive data patterns
Excludes notes and folders through frontmatter and path rules
Auto-masks on idle timeout or window blur
disambiguation: Not an encryption or file-protection tool; it only changes how characters look on screen inside Obsidian.
extras: Visual deterrent only: it does not encrypt notes or protect files on disk. Runs fully locally with no network requests or telemetry; MIT licensed.
motivation: Built so people can write in open offices, flights, cafes or classrooms without wandering eyes reading their notes.
problem: Notes are fully visible on screen, so anyone nearby can read them while writing in shared or public spaces.
summary: Animated visual masking layer that turns completed words into glyphs on screen while leaving the Markdown file unchanged.
